summary: US-017: Seat-level claims — reserved seating enters the core
description:
### US-017: Seat-level claims — reserved seating enters the core
**As** a buyer, **I want** to hold specific seats, not just a quantity, with oversell impossible
per seat. **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** TKT-3 (a seat map to claim against — hard blocker)
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] The claim core accepts a seat-set claim against a seated slot: each seat is held/confirmed
      by at most one live claim (DB-enforced), reusing the ADR-010 lifecycle, lock order,
      idempotency and TTL machinery — the primitive extends, it does not fork (ADR-005 /
      ADR-010 "seats reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource
      constraints").
- [ ] GA and seated pools coexist; the existing GA path is untouched (M1 tests green).
- [ ] Seat-map versioning interplay (TKT-3 COS: edits never orphan or duplicate sold/held seats)
      is honored from the inventory side: a claim pins the seats it named regardless of later map
      edits.
- [ ] The contention test gains a seated variant: ≫C claimants targeting overlapping seat sets;
      no seat is ever double-held.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- Money/ticket-path: audit-trail invariants hold (ADR-003)
- Read-endpoint changes: ADR-004 TTL tier declared with rationale

Parent epic: TKT-4. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §TKT-4.

objective.note: Reserved seating enters the claim core: hold specific seats with per-seat no-oversell.

scope.note: IN: seat-set claims on seated slots, DB-enforced one-live-claim-per-seat, GA path untouched, claims pin seats across map edits, seated contention test. OUT: the seat-map model/designer itself (TKT-3), best-available (US-018), storefront seat picker (TKT-35).

uncertainties.note: Seat identity/versioning shape is TKT-3's output — this ticket consumes it; claim-side schema settles in Planning once TKT-3's model exists.

dependencies.note: HARD blocker: TKT-3 (wired blocked-by). Not claimable until a seat map exists to claim against.

approach.note: Seat-claim rows under the same pool→claim lock order with a uniqueness constraint on (seat, live-status); adapter per ADR-010's stated extension path.

first_slice.note: Hold seats A1–A4 on a seated slot; a racing claim for A3 rejects; GA slots unaffected.

success.note: The 4 ACs + quality gates; the overlapping-seat-set contention test is the load-bearing signal.

binding.rule: The inventory database is the sole write-side correctness boundary. Each mutation locks the inventory pool row first, then its claim rows; operations addressed by hold ID discover the pool with a non-locking read, then re-read the claim after locking the pool — every path has the same pool-to-claim lock order. A claim is held, confirmed, released, or expired; the last three are terminal. PostgreSQL time decides expiry: a transaction expires due holds before capacity accounting, so cleanup jobs are optional optimizations. Confirmed plus unexpired-held quantity may never exceed pool capacity. Hold creation requires an organizer-scoped idempotency key, single-use across the claim's full lifecycle. Reserved seats, date ranges, and entitlements reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints.

Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

governingAdrs.why: Seats 'reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints' — the seat-uniqueness constraint is DB-enforced inside the same transaction shape, not a new primitive.
The claim primitive does not fork: seated is an adapter over the same core, or the unified-model bet fails.
Seat claims count admissions sold — still no occupancy gauge.

reference.summary: PRD v1 §TKT-4 decomposition — the story text is the source of truth
TKT-3 epic — the seat-map model this claims against; its versioning COS is the interplay named in the ACs
